title: Amniotic fluid dynamics: oligohydramnios, polyhydramnios, Potter sequence, amnioinfusion and amnioreduction
subject: ss-obg
refs: SMFM Consult Series #46: Evaluation and management of polyhydramnios
ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 229: Antepartum Fetal Surveillance

steps.say: Amniotic fluid volume changes dynamically throughout gestation to support normal fetal movement and lung expansion. The fluid volume reaches a peak volume of approximately 800 to 1000 milliliters at 34 to 36 weeks gestation, before undergoing a steady physiological decline to 400 to 600 milliliters in post-term pregnancies beyond 41 weeks.
steps.tx: Normal **amniotic fluid volume** peaks progressively to reach a **peak volume** of 800 to 1000 mL at 34 to 36 weeks of gestation. Thereafter, volume steadily decreases to 400 to 600 mL at **post-term** gestations beyond 41 weeks, increasing the risk of cord compression.

steps.say: Mid-gestational fluid balance shifts entirely from maternal transudation to active fetal physiological processes. After 16 weeks gestation, fetal urination and fetal swallowing become the dominant regulatory mechanisms governing fluid turnover and maintaining stable hydrostatic equilibrium.
steps.tx: From 16 weeks gestation onwards, **fetal urination** serves as the primary fluid source (producing up to 1000 mL daily at term), while **fetal swallowing** acts as the major resorption pathway, creating continuous **turnover** that maintains dynamic equilibrium within the gestational sac.

rows: Diffusion across fetal vessels into blood

steps.say: Ultrasound quantification of amniotic fluid guides crucial clinical delivery decisions. Clinicians define oligohydramnios by an amniotic fluid index of 5 centimeters or less across four quadrants, or a single deepest vertical pocket measuring under 2 centimeters.
steps.tx: Sonographic criteria define **oligohydramnios** when the four-quadrant **amniotic fluid index** measures 5 cm or less, or when the single **deepest vertical pocket** measures under 2 cm, signaling diminished uteroplacental perfusion, post-term placental senescence, rupture of fetal membranes, or underlying fetal genitourinary compromise.

nodes.label: Assess four-quadrant fluid sum (AFI) and single deepest pocket (DVP)
AFI <= 5 cm or DVP < 2 cm confirmed
Diagnose oligohydramnios and initiate targeted fetal workup

steps.say: Severe fluid restriction during canalicular lung development provokes life-threatening anatomical distortions. Severe prolonged oligohydramnios before 20 weeks gestation leads to Potter sequence, characterized by fatal pulmonary hypoplasia, compressed facial features, clubbed feet, and bilateral renal agenesis.
steps.tx: Profound early oligohydramnios before 20 weeks gestation results in lethal **Potter sequence**, characterized by fatal **pulmonary hypoplasia**, flattened compressed facies, severe clubbed feet, and progressive musculoskeletal contractures typically secondary to bilateral **renal agenesis**, multicystic dysplastic kidneys, or prolonged pre-viable membrane rupture.

left.title: Early Oligohydramnios (<20 weeks)
points: Arrests alveolar development causing fatal pulmonary hypoplasia
Bilateral renal agenesis, multicystic dysplastic kidneys, or PPROM

right.title: Late Oligohydramnios (>34 weeks)
points: Major risk is umbilical cord compression and fetal hypoxia
Uteroplacental insufficiency, preeclampsia, or post-term gestation

steps.say: Excessive accumulation of fluid introduces significant maternal and fetal perinatal risks. Sonographic evaluation establishes polyhydramnios when the amniotic fluid index reaches 24 to 25 centimeters or higher, or when the deepest vertical pocket measures 8 centimeters or greater.
steps.tx: Clinical **polyhydramnios** is defined on ultrasound by an **amniotic fluid index** of 24 to 25 cm or greater, or a single **deepest vertical pocket** measuring 8 cm or greater. This excessive accumulation predisposes mothers to preterm labour, maternal respiratory distress, fetal malpresentation, cord prolapse, and sudden placental abruption upon membrane rupture.

nodes.label: Assess uterine fundal height disproportionately large for dates
Ultrasound measures DVP >= 8 cm or AFI >= 24 to 25 cm
Stratify severity: mild (8 to 9.9 cm), moderate (10 to 11.9 cm), severe (>= 12 cm)
Investigate maternal diabetes, fetal GI obstruction, and hydrops

steps.say: Investigating polyhydramnios requires a disciplined search for maternal metabolic disease and fetal anatomical lesions. Major etiologies include poorly controlled maternal diabetes, gastrointestinal tract atresias such as duodenal atresia or tracheoesophageal fistula, neural tube defects, and immune or non-immune fetal hydrops.
steps.tx: The clinical etiology of excessive amniotic fluid involves maternal conditions like **maternal diabetes** promoting fetal osmotic diuresis, upper gastrointestinal anomalies like **duodenal atresia** or **tracheoesophageal fistula** preventing normal swallowing, neuromuscular swallowing failure, and high-output fetal cardiac failure causing non-immune hydrops fetalis in utero.

left.title: Fetal Gastrointestinal Causes
points: Duodenal atresia with classic double-bubble sign
Mechanical failure of amniotic fluid resorption

right.title: Maternal and Non-GI Causes
points: Maternal diabetes causing fetal hyperglycemia and polyuria
Anencephaly and spina bifida with transudate leakage
Non-immune hydrops from parvovirus, CMV, or alpha-thalassemia

steps.say: Severe maternal breathlessness from uterine overdistension necessitates urgent invasive decompression. Clinicians perform therapeutic amnioreduction under continuous ultrasound guidance for symptomatic polyhydramnios, carefully draining 1000 to 1500 milliliters per session to relieve maternal respiratory compromise.
steps.tx: In cases of **symptomatic polyhydramnios** presenting with severe maternal orthopnoea or abdominal pain, therapeutic **amnioreduction** under real-time **ultrasound guidance** removes 1000 to 1500 mL per session slowly (under 1000 mL/hr) to avoid sudden uterine decompression, acute maternal hypotension, and premature placental abruption.

rows: Limit aspiration rate to prevent abruption
Twice-weekly NST and umbilical artery Doppler
Assess for hydrops or cord prolapse

steps.say: Intrapartum oligohydramnios exposes the umbilical cord to recurrent mechanical compression between fetal parts and the contracting uterine wall. Infusing warm normal saline through an intrauterine catheter cushions the cord, successfully abolishing repetitive variable decelerations and reducing emergent operative interventions.
steps.tx: Transvaginal **amnioinfusion** using warmed sterile isotonic saline infuses fluid into the uterine cavity to cushion against umbilical **cord compression**, effectively eliminating repetitive intrapartum **variable decelerations**, improving fetal acid-base balance, and significantly lowering emergency cesarean delivery rates during labour without increasing chorioamnionitis.
